description.narrative:
Assessment of Project Outcomes Stakeholder effects Increased access to mortgage finance for homebuyers: Currently, the housing gap is estimated to be around 633,800 housing units. To ease the existing housing gap in the market by making housing finance more accessible, BHS intends to increase its mortgage portfolio for low to middle-income households. Stakeholder effects Increased access to developer finance for green and affordable housing: Senegals housing deficit is projected to grow by around 12,000 housing units per year or about 181,000 additional units by 2030. The proposed IFC funding and advisory services will help BHS increase access to funding to developers operating in the affordable segment. The Project seeks to increase affordable housing units over at least five green-certified projects over the next seven years.
Assessment of Project Outcomes
Competitiveness: By building upon the current regulatory work by the Government of Senegal and the World Bank Group to ease the constraints to develop the housing sector in Senegal and by offering synchronized financing for both supply- and demand-side players to BHS, the Project provides a replicable housing finance model that could trigger a significant shift in the underdeveloped housing market in Senegal. This is expected to send a positive signal to the market regarding the commercial viability of the affordable housing segment. IFC expects other Banks to enter the housing finance market, particularly focusing on the untapped lower end of the commercial market spectrum.

The Project consists of a multi-phase investment package in the amount of US$38.5 million to Banque de lHabitat du Senegal (BHS or the Bank), the leading housing finance bank in the country, to increase access to mortgages for low to middle income families and support developers to build more green and affordable houses. The first phase of the project consists in a debt instrument and subsequent investments might include debt, equity or quasi-equity instruments, to be decided upon and approved at a later date. The use of proceeds is earmarked for affordable housing retail mortgages and/or lending to developers.
